records.gloss: I [am] a crocus of the Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
pieces: I am a crocus of Sharon, \q a lily of the valleys.

L.1: I [am] a crocus of Sharon, \q a lily of the valleys.

R.1: I am a crocus from the plain of Sharon, \q a lily from the valleys.

decisions.choice: the woman speaks
decisions.reason: She speaks of herself as a flower; in 2:2 the man takes up her word "lily" and applies it to her.

decisions.choice: crocus: a flower of the meadows
decisions.reason: The flower named here (chavatselet) grows in the plain and the desert (Isaiah 35:1-2). It was probably a crocus, an asphodel or a narcissus; it was not a rose. "The rose of Sharon" is the familiar older rendering.

decisions.choice: Sharon: the coastal plain
decisions.reason: Sharon is the fertile plain along the coast from Joppa north to Mount Carmel, known for its pastures and wild flowers (Isaiah 35:2; 1 Chronicles 27:29).

decisions.choice: lily: a showy wild flower
decisions.reason: The word (shoshannah) names a bright flower, probably a lily, perhaps a lotus or another flower of the fields. Lilies return through the Song (2:16; 4:5; 5:13; 6:2-3; 7:3). She may be saying that she is a simple wild flower, or that she is lovely; the words allow both.

decisions.choice: from the plain of Sharon ... from the valleys
decisions.reason: Readable says that Sharon is a plain (m3).

records.heading: A lily among thorns

records.source: כְּשֽׁוֹשַׁנָּה֙ בֵּ֣ין הַחוֹחִ֔ים כֵּ֥ן רַעְיָתִ֖י בֵּ֥ין הַבָּנֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Like a lily among the thorns, so [is] my companion among the daughters.
pieces: Like a lily among thorns, \q so is my darling among the young women.

L.2: Like a lily among the thorns, \q so [is] my companion among the daughters.

R.2: My darling, compared with the other young women, \q you are like a lily among thorns.

decisions.choice: the man answers her
decisions.reason: He speaks of "my companion" (1:9) and takes up her word "lily" (2:1).

decisions.choice: a lily among thorns: she outshines all other women
decisions.reason: Next to her, other young women are like thornbushes beside a flower. "Daughters" here means young women in general.

decisions.choice: My darling ... you are like
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to her directly, as the man does in 2:10, to keep the comparison simple.

records.source: כְּתַפּ֨וּחַ֙ בַּעֲצֵ֣י הַיַּ֔עַר כֵּ֥ן דּוֹדִ֖י בֵּ֣ין הַבָּנִ֑ים בְּצִלּוֹ֙ חִמַּ֣דְתִּי וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי וּפִרְי֖וֹ מָת֥וֹק לְחִכִּֽי׃
records.gloss: Like an apple tree among [the] trees of the forest, so [is] my beloved among the sons; in his shade I delighted and sat, and his fruit [is] sweet to my palate.
pieces: As an apple tree stands among the trees of the woods, \q so my beloved stands among the young men. \q With delight I sat down in his shade, \q and his fruit was sweet in my mouth.

L.3: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, \q so [is] my beloved among the young men. \q In his shade I took delight and sat down, \q and his fruit [was] sweet to my palate.

R.3: My love is like an apple tree among the trees of a forest; \q that is how he stands out among the young men. \q I loved to sit in his shade. \q His fruit tasted sweet to me.

decisions.choice: the woman answers in the same way
decisions.reason: She speaks of "my beloved" and answers his comparison (2:2) with one of her own.

decisions.choice: apple tree: a fruit tree, rare and welcome among wild trees
decisions.reason: The tree (tappuach) was probably the apple, though some think of the apricot or quince. Among the wild trees of a forest it is the one that gives shade, scent and sweet fruit (2:5; 7:9; 8:5).

decisions.choice: his shade ... his fruit: the delight of being with him
decisions.reason: To sit in someone's shade is to rest near them, under their care (Psalm 121:5; Hosea 14:8). His fruit, sweet to taste, is the pleasure of his love. The image is kept as an image.

decisions.choice: I took delight and sat down: I sat down with delight
decisions.reason: Two verbs joined by "and" make one action: she sat in his shade and loved it.

decisions.choice: stands ... stands
decisions.reason: Balanced repeats "stands" to make the two halves of the comparison match; Literal keeps the short "so is".

records.source: הֱבִיאַ֨נִי֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַיָּ֔יִן וְדִגְל֥וֹ עָלַ֖י אַהֲבָֽה׃
records.gloss: He brought me to [the] house of the wine, and his banner over me [is] love.
pieces: He has taken me into the banquet hall, \q and the banner he raises over me is love.

L.4: He has brought me to the house of the wine, \q and his banner over me [is] love.

R.4: He took me to the place where wine is served, \q and he shows everyone that he loves me.

decisions.choice: the house of wine: a place of feasting
decisions.reason: The phrase occurs only here; it means a hall where wine is served at a feast, or a vineyard. It is a place of celebration.

decisions.choice: his banner over me is love: his love is displayed over her for all to see
alternatives: his look toward me is love
his intention toward me is love
decisions.reason: The word (degel) is a banner or standard carried over a group of people (Numbers 2:2-3). Raised over her, his love marks her as his. Some connect the word with a related word meaning "to look", and read "his look toward me is love" or "his intention toward me is love".

decisions.choice: he shows everyone that he loves me
alternatives: his banner over me is love
decisions.reason: Readable says what the banner means (m2).

records.source: סַמְּכ֨וּנִי֙ בָּֽאֲשִׁישׁ֔וֹת רַפְּד֖וּנִי בַּתַּפּוּחִ֑ים כִּי־חוֹלַ֥ת אַהֲבָ֖ה אָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Sustain me with raisin cakes, refresh me with apples, for sick of love [am] I.
pieces: Strengthen me with raisin cakes; \q revive me with apples, \q for I am faint with love.

L.5: Sustain me with raisin cakes; \q refresh me with apples, \q for I [am] sick with love.

R.5: Give me raisin cakes to make me strong. \q Give me apples to refresh me. \q I am weak with love.

decisions.choice: she calls to a group
decisions.reason: The commands are plural; she turns to others, probably the women of Jerusalem (2:7).

decisions.choice: raisin cakes ... apples: food for a feast and for the faint
decisions.reason: Raisin cakes were pressed dried grapes, eaten at festivals (2 Samuel 6:19; Hosea 3:1). Apples recall the tree of 2:3; she asks for the very thing that is making her faint.

decisions.choice: sick with love: weak with longing
decisions.reason: Her desire is so strong that she feels faint and unwell (5:8).

records.gloss: His left hand [is] under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
pieces: His left arm is under my head, \q and his right arm holds me close.

L.6: His left hand [is] under my head, \q and his right hand embraces me.

R.6: His left arm is under my head, \q and his right arm holds me close.

decisions.choice: a statement, or a wish
alternatives: Let his left hand be under my head, and let his right hand embrace me
decisions.reason: The sentence has no main verb in its first half, and the second verb can describe what is happening or what she longs for: "let his left hand be under my head". The same words return in 8:3.

decisions.choice: an embrace as they lie together
decisions.reason: One arm under her head and the other around her: the lovers lie in each other's arms.

decisions.choice: arm
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses "hand" for the whole hand and arm; Balanced and Readable say "arm", which is what an embrace uses.

records.source: הִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בְּנ֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ בִּצְבָא֔וֹת א֖וֹ בְּאַיְל֣וֹת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה אִם־תָּעִ֧ירוּ׀וְֽאִם־תְּעֽוֹרְר֛וּ אֶת־הָאַהֲבָ֖ה עַ֥ד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּֽץ׃ס
records.gloss: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by [the] gazelles or by [the] does of the field: if you stir up and if you awaken the love until it pleases.
pieces: Swear to me, women of Jerusalem, by the gazelles \q or by the does in the fields: \q do not stir up or awaken love until it is ready.

L.7: I put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles \q or by the does of the field: \q do not stir up and do not awaken love until it pleases.

R.7: Women of Jerusalem, promise me \q by the gazelles and the wild deer: \q Do not stir up love or wake it until the time is right.

decisions.choice: the woman puts the women of Jerusalem under oath
decisions.reason: "I make you swear" is her word to the women; the same oath, with the same words, comes in 3:5 and 8:4 and closes a section each time.

decisions.choice: by the gazelles or the does of the field: an oath by the wild creatures of love
decisions.reason: People swore by God or by something precious. Here the oath is by graceful wild animals, which belong to the world of the Song (2:9, 17). The words for "gazelles" and "does of the field" sound like two titles of God, "of hosts" and "God Almighty", and some see a playful echo of an oath by God; this is uncertain.

decisions.choice: if you stir up ...: do not stir up
decisions.reason: In a Hebrew oath, "if you do this" means "you must not do this" (the end of the curse is left unsaid, Genesis 21:23).

decisions.choice: do not stir up love until it pleases: do not rouse love before its time
alternatives: do not disturb the lovers until they wish
decisions.reason: The oath asks the women not to awaken love, or stir up desire, before love itself is ready. Some read it instead as "do not disturb us": do not rouse the lovers until love is satisfied. The same words return in 3:5 and 8:4.

decisions.choice: until it pleases: until love itself wishes
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine, and its subject is "love", also feminine: love has its own time. It could also be read "until she pleases", of the woman, but love is the nearer subject.

decisions.choice: one wording for the oath in 2:7, 3:5 and 8:4
decisions.reason: The three oaths are worded alike at each level, so that the reader hears the refrain: Literal "I put you under oath ... do not stir up and do not awaken love until it pleases"; Balanced "Swear to me ... do not stir up or awaken love until it is ready"; Readable "promise me ... Do not stir up love or wake it until the time is right".

decisions.choice: women of Jerusalem

records.source: ק֣וֹל דּוֹדִ֔י הִנֵּה־זֶ֖ה בָּ֑א מְדַלֵּג֙ עַל־הֶ֣הָרִ֔ים מְקַפֵּ֖ץ עַל־הַגְּבָעֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: [The] voice of my beloved! Look, this [one] comes, leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills.
pieces: Listen! My beloved! \q Look, here he comes, \q leaping over the mountains, \q bounding over the hills.

L.8: The voice of my beloved! \q Look, here he comes, \q leaping over the mountains, \q bounding over the hills.

R.8: Listen! I hear my love! \q Look, here he comes, \q leaping over the mountains, \q running across the hills.

decisions.choice: the woman speaks (2:8-17)
decisions.reason: She speaks of "my beloved"; a new scene begins as he comes to her house.

decisions.choice: the voice of: listen!
decisions.reason: The word for "voice" or "sound" at the head of a sentence works as a cry: "Listen!" (Isaiah 40:3, 6; 52:8). She hears him before she sees him.

decisions.choice: leaping ... bounding: as a deer runs
decisions.reason: The verbs picture the quick, springing run of a gazelle or stag (2:9; Isaiah 35:6). He is eager, and no distance holds him back.

records.heading: Come away, my darling

records.source: דּוֹמֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ לִצְבִ֔י א֖וֹ לְעֹ֣פֶר הָֽאַיָּלִ֑ים הִנֵּה־זֶ֤ה עוֹמֵד֙ אַחַ֣ר כָּתְלֵ֔נוּ מַשְׁגִּ֨יחַ֙ מִן־הַֽחֲלֹּנ֔וֹת מֵצִ֖יץ מִן־הַֽחֲרַכִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Like is my beloved to a gazelle or to a young one of the stags; look, this [one] stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattices.
pieces: My beloved is like a gazelle \q or a young stag. \q There he stands behind our wall, \q looking in through the windows, \q peering through the lattice.

L.9: My beloved is like a gazelle \q or a young one of the stags. \q Look, this [one] is standing behind our wall, \q gazing through the windows, \q peering through the lattices.

R.9: My love is like a gazelle \q or a young deer. \q Look, he is standing outside the wall of our house. \q He is looking in through the windows, \q peering through the lattice.

decisions.choice: a gazelle or a young stag: swift, graceful and wild
decisions.reason: Gazelles and deer were the image of speed and grace in the hills (2 Samuel 2:18; Proverbs 6:5). The comparison returns in 2:17 and 8:14.

decisions.choice: our wall ... the windows ... the lattice: the house where she lives
decisions.reason: "Our wall" is the wall of her family's house. Windows had no glass; the lattice was a screen of crossed wooden bars over the opening (Judges 5:28). He looks in, she looks out.

records.source: עָנָ֥ה דוֹדִ֖י וְאָ֣מַר לִ֑י ק֥וּמִי לָ֛ךְ רַעְיָתִ֥י יָפָתִ֖י וּלְכִי־לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Answered my beloved and said to me: Arise for yourself, my companion, my beautiful one, and come for yourself.
pieces: My beloved spoke to me and said, \q "Get up, my darling, my beautiful one, and come away.

L.10: My beloved answered and said to me, \q "Rise up, my companion, my beautiful one, and come away.

R.10: My love spoke to me. He said, \q "Get up, my darling! My beautiful one, come with me.

decisions.choice: she reports what he said to her (2:10-13)
decisions.reason: The woman is still the speaker; she quotes the man's words to her. His words run to the end of 2:13, where his call is repeated.

decisions.choice: answered and said: spoke
decisions.reason: "Answered" often means simply that someone began to speak; it need not reply to a question (Job 3:2).

decisions.choice: rise up for yourself ... come for yourself
decisions.reason: Each command is followed by "for yourself", which adds warmth and urgency (as 1:8). He invites her to leave the house and come out with him.

decisions.choice: my beautiful one
decisions.reason: A feminine word for "beautiful" used as a name, as the women also call her "most beautiful" (1:8).

decisions.choice: quotation marks
decisions.reason: The Song's speeches take no quotation marks, but a speech quoted inside a speech does: she quotes his words here, so they stand in double quotation marks to the end of 2:13.

decisions.choice: come with me
decisions.reason: Readable says where she is called to come.

records.source: כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֥ה הַסְּתָ֖יו עָבָ֑ר הַגֶּ֕שֶׁם חָלַ֖ף הָלַ֥ךְ לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For look, the winter has passed; the rain is over, it has gone for itself.
pieces: For see, the winter is past; \q the rain is over and gone.

L.11: For look, the winter has passed; \q the rain is over [and] gone.

R.11: Winter is past. \q The rains are over and gone.

decisions.choice: winter ... the rain: the rainy season
decisions.reason: In Israel the rains fall from about October to April; when they stop, spring comes. The word for winter occurs only here.

records.source: הַנִּצָּנִים֙ נִרְא֣וּ בָאָ֔רֶץ עֵ֥ת הַזָּמִ֖יר הִגִּ֑יעַ וְק֥וֹל הַתּ֖וֹר נִשְׁמַ֥ע בְּאַרְצֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: The blossoms appear in the land; [the] time of the singing has come, and [the] voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
pieces: Flowers are appearing in the land; \q the season of singing has come, \q and the cooing of the turtledove is heard in our land.

L.12: The blossoms have appeared in the land; \q the time of singing has arrived, \q and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.

R.12: Flowers are blooming everywhere. \q It is time to sing. \q The turtledoves are cooing in our land.

decisions.choice: singing: the season of song
decisions.reason: The word can mean "singing" or "pruning" (the trimming of vines in spring). Both fit spring; next to the song of the dove, singing is the likelier sense, and the sound may be heard as both.

decisions.choice: the turtledove: a bird that returns in spring
decisions.reason: The turtledove migrates and comes back each spring (Jeremiah 8:7); its cooing is a sign that the season has turned.

records.source: הַתְּאֵנָה֙ חָֽנְטָ֣ה פַגֶּ֔יהָ וְהַגְּפָנִ֥ים׀סְמָדַ֖ר נָ֣תְנוּ רֵ֑יחַ ק֥וּמִי לָ֛ךְ רַעְיָתִ֥י יָפָתִ֖י וּלְכִי־לָֽךְ׃ס
records.gloss: The fig tree has ripened its early figs, and the vines [in] blossom have given fragrance. Arise, come for yourself, my companion, my beautiful one, and come for yourself.
pieces: The fig tree is ripening its early figs, \q and the blossoming vines spread their fragrance. \q Get up, my darling, my beautiful one, and come away."

L.13: The fig tree has ripened its early figs, \q and the vines in blossom have given fragrance. \q Rise up, my companion, my beautiful one, and come away."

R.13: The first figs are growing on the fig trees. \q The grapevines are blooming and smell sweet. \q Get up, my darling! My beautiful one, come with me."

decisions.choice: early figs: the first small figs of spring
decisions.reason: The fig tree puts out small green figs in spring, before its leaves are full; they ripen later (Matthew 24:32). The vines are in flower and give off a faint sweet scent.

decisions.choice: has ripened
decisions.reason: The verb is used elsewhere of embalming with spices (Genesis 50:2); here it seems to mean that the figs ripen and grow sweet.

decisions.choice: his call is repeated
decisions.reason: The closing line repeats the call of 2:10, and his quoted words end here.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2:10
decisions.reason: The repeated call is worded as in 2:10 at each level, so the refrain can be heard.

records.source: יוֹנָתִ֞י בְּחַגְוֵ֣י הַסֶּ֗לַע בְּסֵ֨תֶר֙ הַמַּדְרֵגָ֔ה הַרְאִ֨ינִי֙ אֶתּ־מַרְאַ֔יִךְהַשְׁמִיעִ֖ינִי אֶת־קוֹלֵ֑ךְ כִּי־קוֹלֵ֥ךְ עָרֵ֖ב וּמַרְאֵ֥יךְ נָאוֶֽה׃ס
records.gloss: My dove, in [the] clefts of the rock, in [the] hiding place of the cliff, let me see your form, let me hear your voice, for your voice [is] sweet and your form lovely.
pieces: My dove, hidden in the clefts of the rock, in the shelter of the cliff, \q show me your face, \q let me hear you speak, \q for your voice is sweet and your face is lovely.

L.14: My dove, in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding place of the cliff, \q let me see your form, \q let me hear your voice, \q because your voice [is] sweet, and your form [is] lovely.

R.14: My dove, you are like a dove hiding in the cracks of the rocks, high on a cliff. \q Let me see your face. \q Let me hear your voice. \q Your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.

decisions.choice: the man speaks
alternatives: the woman still reports his words
decisions.reason: He speaks to her with feminine forms and calls her "my dove". This may be the man speaking for himself, or still part of the words the woman reports from 2:10-13; the Hebrew does not mark where a quotation ends.

decisions.choice: a dove in the clefts of the rock: hidden and out of reach
decisions.reason: Rock doves nest in cracks high on cliffs (Jeremiah 48:28). He cannot reach her where she is hidden, and asks her to show herself.

decisions.choice: your form: your appearance, your face
decisions.reason: The word means how someone looks: the face, or the whole person.

decisions.choice: your face
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "face", what he longs to see at the window; Literal keeps the wider "form".

decisions.choice: you are like a dove hiding
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture of the dove (m2).

records.heading: My dove in the clefts of the rock

records.source: אֶֽחֱזוּ־לָ֨נוּ֙ שֽׁוּעָלִ֔ים שֽׁוּעָלִ֥ים קְטַנִּ֖ים מְחַבְּלִ֣ים כְּרָמִ֑ים וּכְרָמֵ֖ינוּ סְמָדַֽר׃
records.gloss: Catch for us foxes, little foxes, ruining vineyards, and our vineyards [are in] blossom.
pieces: Catch the foxes for us, \q the little foxes that spoil vineyards, \q for our vineyards are blossoming.

L.15: Catch for us foxes, \q little foxes that ruin vineyards, \q for our vineyards [are in] blossom.

R.15: Catch the foxes for us, \q the little foxes that damage the vineyards. \q Our vineyards are blooming.

decisions.choice: who speaks is not clear
decisions.reason: The command is plural and the vineyards are "ours". It may be the woman answering his wish to hear her voice (2:14) with a song, the man, the two together, or her brothers, who keep the vineyards (1:6).

decisions.choice: foxes that ruin vineyards
decisions.reason: Foxes, or jackals (the same word covers both), dug among the vines and ate the grapes (Judges 15:4; Nehemiah 3:35).

decisions.choice: little foxes ... our vineyards in blossom: what threatens young love
decisions.reason: The vineyard stands for the woman and her love (1:6). The foxes may be whatever could spoil love while it is still in flower, or young men who come after the young women; the image is kept, and its meaning is uncertain.

records.heading: The little foxes

records.source: דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ הָרֹעֶ֖ה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃
records.gloss: My beloved [is] mine and I [am] his, who pastures among the lilies.
pieces: My beloved is mine, and I am his; \q he grazes among the lilies.

L.16: My beloved [is] mine, and I [am] his, \q who pastures among the lilies.

R.16: My love belongs to me, and I belong to him. \q He feeds among the lilies.

decisions.choice: the woman speaks
decisions.reason: She speaks of "my beloved" and of herself.

decisions.choice: my beloved is mine and I am his: they belong to each other
decisions.reason: The short balanced lines say that the bond goes both ways. She says it again in 6:3 and, in another form, in 7:11.

decisions.choice: who pastures among the lilies: who grazes his flock, or himself feeds, among the lilies
alternatives: who grazes his flock among the lilies
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to feed a flock or to graze. He may be the shepherd among the flowers, or the gazelle (2:17) feeding there. Since she is the lily (2:1-2), the picture is also of his delight in her (4:5; 6:2-3).

records.source: עַ֤ד שֶׁיָּפ֨וּחַ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְנָ֖סוּ הַצְּלָלִ֑ים סֹב֩ דְּמֵה־לְךָ֨דוֹדִ֜י לִצְבִ֗י א֛וֹ לְעֹ֥פֶר הָאַיָּלִ֖ים עַל־הָ֥רֵי בָֽתֶר׃ס
records.gloss: Until that breathes the day and flee the shadows, turn, be like, my beloved, to a gazelle or to a young one of the stags on [the] mountains of Bether.
pieces: Until the day breathes \q and the shadows flee, \q turn, my beloved, be like a gazelle or a young stag on Bether's mountains.

L.17: Until the day breathes \q and the shadows flee, \q turn, be like, my beloved, a gazelle or a young one of the stags on the mountains of Bether.

R.17: Until the day breathes \q and the shadows run away, \q turn, my love, and be like a gazelle or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.

decisions.choice: until the day breathes and the shadows flee: evening, or the dawn
decisions.reason: The day "breathes" when a breeze rises. That may be the cool wind of evening, when shadows grow long and disappear (Genesis 3:8), or the breeze of dawn, when the shadows of night flee. The words keep both.

decisions.choice: turn: come back to me, or turn away
decisions.reason: She may ask him to turn to her and be like a gazelle on the "mountains", spending the night with her, or to go away until the day comes. The verb allows both.

decisions.choice: the mountains of Bether: a place, or "divided mountains"
decisions.reason: No place called Bether is known for certain. The word may mean "division" or "cleft": mountains cut by ravines. Some take it as a name for her body. It is kept as a name, Bether; compare 8:14, "mountains of spices".

decisions.choice: she speaks to him
decisions.reason: "Turn" and "be like" are masculine; she speaks to her beloved.
